No route returns, re-renders or logs a password.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Form, HTTPException, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n\nfrom app import accounts\nfrom app.permissions import require\nfrom app.web import render\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/admin/users\")\n\n\ndef _db(request: Request):\n    return request.app.state.database\n\n\ndef _account_url(request: Request, user_id: int) -> str:\n    return request.app.url_path_for(\"account_page\", user_id=user_id)\n\n\ndef _status_for(error: accounts.AccountError) -> int:\n    if isinstance(error, accounts.NoSuchAccount):\n        return 404\n    if isinstance(error, (accounts.UsernameTaken, accounts.WouldLockOutAdmins)):\n        return 409\n    return 400\n\n\ndef _new_form(request: Request, *, status_code=200, **context):\n    return render(request, \"admin/user_new.html\", status_code=status_code,\n                  title=\"New account\", user=request.state.user, roles=accounts.ROLES,\n                  username_value=\"\", display_name_value=\"\", role_value=\"editor\",\n                  **context)\n\n\ndef _account(request: Request, user_id: int, *, status_code=200, **context):\n    account = accounts.get_user(_db(request), user_id)\n    if account is None:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=\"No such account.\")\n    return render(request, \"admin/user_detail.html\", status_code=status_code,\n                  title=\"Account\", user=request.state.user, account=account,\n                  roles=accounts.ROLES, **context)\n\n\ndef _apply(request: Request, user_id: int, change, *, error_key: str):\n    \"\"\"Run an account change; on success go back to the account, else show why.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        change()\n    except accounts.NoSuchAccount:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=\"No such account.\") from None\n    except accounts.AccountError as error:\n        return _account(request, user_id, status_code=_status_for(error),\n                        **{error_key: str(error)})\n    return RedirectResponse(_account_url(request, user_id), status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.get(\"\", dependencies=[Depends(require(\"user.list\"))])\ndef user_list(request: Request):\n    return render(request, \"admin/user_list.html\", title=\"Accounts\",\n                  user=request.state.user, accounts=accounts.list_accounts(_db(request)))\n\n\n@router.get(\"/new\", dependencies=[Depends(require(\"user.create\"))])\ndef new_user(request: Request):\n    return _new_form(request)\n\n\n@router.post(\"\", dependencies=[Depends(require(\"user.create\"))])\ndef create_user(request: Request, username: str = Form(\"\"), password: str = Form(\"\"),\n                role: str = Form(\"\"), display_name: str = Form(\"\")):\n    try:\n        user_id = accounts.create_account(\n            _db(request), username=username, password=password, role=role,\n            display_name=display_name)\n    except accounts.AccountError as error:\n        # What was typed comes back, except the password, which never does.\n        return _new_form(request, status_code=_status_for(error), error=str(error),\n                         username_value=username, display_name_value=display_name,\n                         role_value=role)\n    return RedirectResponse(_account_url(request, user_id), status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.get(\"/{user_id}\", dependencies=[Depends(require(\"user.view\"))])\ndef account_page(request: Request, user_id: int):\n    return _account(request, user_id)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{user_id}/role\", dependencies=[Depends(require(\"user.change_role\"))])\ndef change_role(request: Request, user_id: int, role: str = Form(\"\")):\n    return _apply(request, user_id,\n                  lambda: accounts.change_role(_db(request), user_id, role),\n                  error_key=\"role_error\")\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{user_id}/deactivate\", dependencies=[Depends(require(\"user.deactivate\"))])\ndef deactivate_user(request: Request, user_id: int):\n    return _apply(request, user_id,\n                  lambda: accounts.deactivate(_db(request), user_id,\n                                              acting_user_id=request.state.user[\"id\"]),\n                  error_key=\"status_error\")\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{user_id}/reactivate\", dependencies=[Depends(require(\"user.reactivate\"))])\ndef reactivate_user(request: Request, user_id: int):\n    return _apply(request, user_id,\n                  lambda: accounts.reactivate(_db(request), user_id),\n                  error_key=\"status_error\")\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{user_id}/password\", dependencies=[Depends(require(\"user.reset_password\"))])\ndef reset_password(request: Request, user_id: int, password: str = Form(\"\")):\n    return _apply(request, user_id,\n                  lambda: accounts.reset_password(_db(request), user_id, password),\n                  error_key=\"password_error\")\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{user_id}/display-name\",\n             dependencies=[Depends(require(\"user.change_display_name\"))])\ndef change_display_name(request: Request, user_id: int, display_name: str = Form(\"\")):\n    return _apply(request, user_id,\n No route returns, re-renders or logs a password.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Form, HTTPException, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n\nfrom app import accounts\nfrom app.permissions import require\nfrom app.web import render\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/admin/users\")\n\n\ndef _db(request: Request):\n    return request.app.state.database\n\n\ndef _account_url(request: Request, user_id: int) -> str:\n    return request.app.url_path_for(\"account_page\", user_id=user_id)\n\n\ndef _status_for(error: accounts.AccountError) -> int:\n    if isinstance(error, accounts.NoSuchAccount):\n        return 404\n    if isinstance(error, (accounts.UsernameTaken, accounts.WouldLockOutAdmins)):\n        return 409\n    return 400\n\n\ndef _new_form(request: Request, *, status_code=200, **context):\n    return render(request, \"admin/user_new.html\", status_code=status_code,\n                  title=\"New account\", user=request.state.user, roles=accounts.ROLES,\n                  username_value=\"\", display_name_value=\"\", role_value=\"editor\",\n                  **context)\n\n\ndef _account(request: Request, user_id: int, *, status_code=200, **context):\n    account = accounts.get_user(_db(request), user_id)\n    if account is None:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=\"No such account.\")\n    return render(request, \"admin/user_detail.html\", status_code=status_code,\n                  title=\"Account\", user=request.state.user, account=account,\n                  roles=accounts.ROLES, **context)\n\n\ndef _apply(request: Request, user_id: int, change, *, error_key: str):\n    \"\"\"Run an account change; on success go back to the account, else show why.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        change()\n    except accounts.NoSuchAccount:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=\"No such account.\") from None\n    except accounts.AccountError as error:\n        return _account(request, user_id, status_code=_status_for(error),\n                        **{error_key: str(error)})\n    return RedirectResponse(_account_url(request, user_id), status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.get(\"\", dependencies=[Depends(require(\"user.list\"))])\ndef user_list(request: Request):\n    return render(request, \"admin/user_list.html\", title=\"Accounts\",\n                  user=request.state.user, accounts=accounts.list_accounts(_db(request)))\n\n\n@router.get(\"/new\", dependencies=[Depends(require(\"user.create\"))])\ndef new_user(request: Request):\n    return _new_form(request)\n\n\n@router.post(\"\", dependencies=[Depends(require(\"user.create\"))])\ndef create_user(request: Request, username: str = Form(\"\"), password: str = Form(\"\"),\n                role: str = Form(\"\"), display_name: str = Form(\"\")):\n    try:\n        user_id = accounts.create_account(\n            _db(request), username=username, password=password, role=role,\n            display_name=display_name)\n    except accounts.AccountError as error:\n        # What was typed comes back, except the password, which never does.\n        return _new_form(request, status_code=_status_for(error), error=str(error),\n                         username_value=username, display_name_value=display_name,\n                         role_value=role)\n    return RedirectResponse(_account_url(request, user_id), status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.get(\"/{user_id}\", dependencies=[Depends(require(\"user.view\"))])\ndef account_page(request: Request, user_id: int):\n    return _account(request, user_id)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{user_id}/role\", dependencies=[Depends(require(\"user.change_role\"))])\ndef change_role(request: Request, user_id: int, role: str = Form(\"\")):\n    return _apply(request, user_id,\n                  lambda: accounts.change_role(_db(request), user_id, role),\n                  error_key=\"role_error\")\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{user_id}/deactivate\", dependencies=[Depends(require(\"user.deactivate\"))])\ndef deactivate_user(request: Request, user_id: int):\n    return _apply(request, user_id,\n                  lambda: accounts.deactivate(_db(request), user_id,\n                                              acting_user_id=request.state.user[\"id\"]),\n                  error_key=\"status_error\")\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{user_id}/reactivate\", dependencies=[Depends(require(\"user.reactivate\"))])\ndef reactivate_user(request: Request, user_id: int):\n    return _apply(request, user_id,\n                  lambda: accounts.reactivate(_db(request), user_id),\n                  error_key=\"status_error\")\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{user_id}/password\", dependencies=[Depends(require(\"user.reset_password\"))])\ndef reset_password(request: Request, user_id: int, password: str = Form(\"\")):\n    return _apply(request, user_id,\n                  lambda: accounts.reset_password(_db(request), user_id, password),\n                  error_key=\"password_error\")\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{user_id}/display-name\",\n             dependencies=[Depends(require(\"user.change_display_name\"))])\ndef change_display_name(request: Request, user_id: int, display_name: str = Form(\"\")):\n    return _apply(request, user_id,\n                  lambda: accounts.change_display_name(_db(request), user_id, display_name),\n {"parentUuid":"36855f12-0584-4d25-a60d-c8d208feebb9","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"a0d67ccc-f1be-44d9-b6fd-cf8b7b8473b4","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/yawoppong-krampah/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: since HEAD (uncommitted T04 work: app/accounts.py, app/routes/users.py, app/permissions.py, app/main.py, templates/admin/user_*.html, dashboard.html, tests/test_t04_users.py) against ticket #5 and spec #1"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"04bfcd41-21f5-449d-b5eb-c030d1e345c9","timestamp":"2026-10-12T04:17:17.640Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01UiGszpsnqmBDyhqkfpcTGC","session_id":"ed24a1e3-881f-4be6-a801-a77028a939ce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"ed24a1e3-881f-4be6-a801-a77028a939ce","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"main"}

The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>**Spec review of the uncommitted T04 change**\n\nI read the diff, issue #5, issue #1, and the CONTEXT.md glossary. I did not run the tests. Every #5 acceptance criterion is implemented, and I found no outright spec violations.\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n- **Existing-session test is loose.** #5 says \"any existing session stops working\". The code is right: `security.current_user` re-reads `active` on every request and clears the session. The test is weaker, because the stale session's POST accepts `status_code in (302, 303, 403)`. It never checks that the POST changed nothing.\n- **No byline test through the Editor's session.** The spec asks for tests of \"every Editor refusal\". Refusal is covered for all 9 routes (list, new, view, create, role, deactivate, reactivate, password, display-name), including for a nonexistent id. Because `require()` runs as a route dependency, permission is checked before lookup.\n- **Nothing important is missing.** Create, role, deactivate/reactivate, password reset, Display name, CSRF on every form, the \"Posts stay Published\" test, and the publish-seam byline tests are all present.\n\n**(b) Scope creep (not in #5 or #1)**\n- **Last-active-Admin guard.** `WouldLockOutAdmins` in `change_role` stops the last active Admin being demoted. Nothing in #1 or #5 asks for it. It is a sensible safety rule, but it adds a 409 path and three tests. If kept, record it in CONTEXT.md.\n- **Self-deactivation block.** `deactivate(..., acting_user_id)` refuses an Admin deactivating themself. This is also unrequested, and it adds a test.\n- **Dashboard \"Accounts\" link.** This is minor and arguably needed for navigation. It is not the story 45 account counts, which correctly were not built.\n- **Username shown on the account list.** The list shows \"signs in as {{ username }}\" and the detail page shows the username. This is Admin-only and labelled private, so it does not breach \"never a byline\". Neither screen is required by the spec.\n\n**(c) Implemented but possibly wrong**\n- **Role changes and password resets do not end the account's sessions.** The spec only requires this for deactivation, so it is not a violation. A reset password on a live session leaves that session valid, which may surprise the Admin.\n- **Reset on a Deactivated account.** This is allowed and does not reactivate it, and the test confirms that. The spec is silent on it. It is fine, but it is a policy choice.\n- **CSRF versus refusal ordering.** CSRF is an app-wide dependency, so an Editor POST with no token gets 403 \"Invalid or missing CSRF token\" instead of the permission page. This is acceptable, because #5 only requires the refusal page for submitted actions that carry a valid session and token.\n\n**Checks that passed**\n- **Password handling.** No route re-renders the password. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>**Spec review of the uncommitted T04 change**\n\nI read the diff, issue #5, issue #1, and the CONTEXT.md glossary. I did not run the tests. Every #5 acceptance criterion is implemented, and I found no outright spec violations.\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n- **Existing-session test is loose.** #5 says \"any existing session stops working\". The code is right: `security.current_user` re-reads `active` on every request and clears the session. The test is weaker, because the stale session's POST accepts `status_code in (302, 303, 403)`. It never checks that the POST changed nothing.\n- **No byline test through the Editor's session.** The spec asks for tests of \"every Editor refusal\". Refusal is covered for all 9 routes (list, new, view, create, role, deactivate, reactivate, password, display-name), including for a nonexistent id. Because `require()` runs as a route dependency, permission is checked before lookup.\n- **Nothing important is missing.** Create, role, deactivate/reactivate, password reset, Display name, CSRF on every form, the \"Posts stay Published\" test, and the publish-seam byline tests are all present.\n\n**(b) Scope creep (not in #5 or #1)**\n- **Last-active-Admin guard.** `WouldLockOutAdmins` in `change_role` stops the last active Admin being demoted. Nothing in #1 or #5 asks for it. It is a sensible safety rule, but it adds a 409 path and three tests. If kept, record it in CONTEXT.md.\n- **Self-deactivation block.** `deactivate(..., acting_user_id)` refuses an Admin deactivating themself. This is also unrequested, and it adds a test.\n- **Dashboard \"Accounts\" link.** This is minor and arguably needed for navigation. It is not the story 45 account counts, which correctly were not built.\n- **Username shown on the account list.** The list shows \"signs in as {{ username }}\" and the detail page shows the username. This is Admin-only and labelled private, so it does not breach \"never a byline\". Neither screen is required by the spec.\n\n**(c) Implemented but possibly wrong**\n- **Role changes and password resets do not end the account's sessions.** The spec only requires this for deactivation, so it is not a violation. A reset password on a live session leaves that session valid, which may surprise the Admin.\n- **Reset on a Deactivated account.** This is allowed and does not reactivate it, and the test confirms that. The spec is silent on it. It is fine, but it is a policy choice.\n- **CSRF versus refusal ordering.** CSRF is an app-wide dependency, so an Editor POST with no token gets 403 \"Invalid or missing CSRF token\" instead of the permission page. This is acceptable, because #5 only requires the refusal page for submitted actions that carry a valid session and token.\n\n**Checks that passed**\n- **Password handling.** No route re-renders the password. Error paths return username, Display name and role only. Hashing goes through `hash_password`, and the caplog tests assert it is not logged.\n- **Accounts never deleted.** There is no delete route or function, and `test_accounts_are_never_deleted` exists.\n- **Byline.** `publish.py` joins `users.display_name AS author_name`, so it follows the current Display name. The username-as-byline test scans the output.\n- **Author link.** `posts.author_id` is never touched.\n\n**Files**\n- /Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/routes/users.py\n- /Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/accounts.py\n- /Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/permissions.py\n- /Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/tests/test_t04_users.py</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>54335</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>9</tool_uses><duration_ms>34363</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>","reason":"absorbed_mid_turn","commandUuid":"cef82aef-7879-4bef-a521-6e8680052bfb","deliveryId":"8beef196-9434-4197-96ed-58ee63dc0627"}

If kept, record it in CONTEXT.md.\n- **Self-deactivation block.** `deactivate(..., acting_user_id)` refuses an Admin deactivating themself. This is also unrequested, and it adds a test.\n- **Dashboard \"Accounts\" link.** This is minor and arguably needed for navigation. It is not the story 45 account counts, which correctly were not built.\n- **Username shown on the account list.** The list shows \"signs in as {{ username }}\" and the detail page shows the username. This is Admin-only and labelled private, so it does not breach \"never a byline\". Neither screen is required by the spec.\n\n**(c) Implemented but possibly wrong**\n- **Role changes and password resets do not end the account's sessions.** The spec only requires this for deactivation, so it is not a violation. A reset password on a live session leaves that session valid, which may surprise the Admin.\n- **Reset on a Deactivated account.** This is allowed and does not reactivate it, and the test confirms that. The spec is silent on it. It is fine, but it is a policy choice.\n- **CSRF versus refusal ordering.** CSRF is an app-wide dependency, so an Editor POST with no token gets 403 \"Invalid or missing CSRF token\" instead of the permission page. This is acceptable, because #5 only requires the refusal page for submitted actions that carry a valid session and token.\n\n**Checks that passed**\n- **Password handling.** No route re-renders the password. Error paths return username, Display name and role only. Hashing goes through `hash_password`, and the caplog tests assert it is not logged.\n- **Accounts never deleted.** There is no delete route or function, and `test_accounts_are_never_deleted` exists.\n- **Byline.** `publish.py` joins `users.display_name AS author_name`, so it follows the current Display name. The username-as-byline test scans the output.\n- **Author link.** `posts.author_id` is never touched.\n\n**Files**\n- /Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/routes/users.py\n- /Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/accounts.py\n- /Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/permissions.py\n- /Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/tests/test_t04_users.py</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>54335</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>9</tool_uses><duration_ms>34363</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>\n</system-reminder>"}],"renderedRole":"system","session_id":"ed24a1e3-881f-4be6-a801-a77028a939ce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"ed24a1e3-881f-4be6-a801-a77028a939ce","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"24a0d0a1-0691-4a3a-9670-5aaeee8580f2","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CfwhXF3gCkE3pofK1SAsG","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"T04 is committed as `e0df28a` on `main`, and the full suite passes (181 tests, 60 of them new). The commit message ends `Closes #5`, but I haven't pushed, so the issue stays open until you do.\n\n**What an Admin can now do** (all under `/admin/users`, linked from the Dashboard):\n- **Create accounts:** with a private username, a password, a role and a public Display name.\n- **Change an account:** its role, or its Display name.\n- **Deactivate and reactivate:** accounts are never deleted. A deactivated account can't sign in, and its existing session stops working on the next request.\n- **Set a new password:** the old one is never shown, and the new one is stored hashed. It never appears in any response or log, including on validation errors.\n- **Bylines:** a Post's byline follows its Author's current Display name on the next `cms publish`. The Author link and Published status survive deactivation and Display name changes.\n- **Editors:** they get the \"You don't have permission\" page on all 9 account screens and actions, including for ids that don't exist.\n- **CSRF:** every account form carries a token.\n\n**How it went**\n- **Tests first:** I wrote the tests first and confirmed 50 failed before writing code. I also flipped one permission rule to check the tests caught it; 3 tests failed, and I restored the rule.\n- **Code review:** it found no hard standards violations and no missing requirements. I fixed the small nits, tightened the loose session test, and posted the findings and resolutions as a comment on #5.\n- **Typechecking:** there's no typechecker in the project's dev dependencies, so I didn't run one. I didn't add one, since new dependencies need your OK.\n\n**Decisions for you**\n- **Lock-out rules (not in the ticket):** an Admin can't deactivate their own account, and the last active Admin can't be demoted. {"parentUuid":"052d0769-8581-4ff0-8ac4-676e0bbe3acb","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"d15658d4-d3ed-49dc-be2f-eeac9afa22b7","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Ut9Ek24hvUXd7n5LW6nD1s","type":"tool_result","content":"To https://github.com/yawoppongkrampah-hub/iphs400-mp2-cms.git\n   06a3070..e0df28a  main -> main\n---\n{\"closedAt\":\"2026-10-12T04:24:20Z\",\"comments\":[{\"createdAt\":\"2026-10-12T04:18:52Z\",\"head\":\"## /code-review findings for T04 (and how each was resolved)\"}],\"state\":\"CLOSED\"}\n---\n## Parent\n\nSpec: #1\n\n## What to build\n\nEditors get a Preview and an Event details hint in the Post and Page editors, and the whole project is made demo-ready and documented. This is a testable vertical slice (route, template and tests) as well as the demo, screenshots and documentation tasks. It must not be completed as documentation alone.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n**Preview and hint (route, template, tests)**\n\n- [ ] The Post editor and the Page editor each have a Preview that shows exactly the content the public page will render, using the same rendering and sanitizing as the export. Raw HTML, scripts, iframes and forms do not run in the Preview.\n- [ ] The Post editor shows a short Event details hint (What, When, Where, Who can attend). The hint is never pre-filled into the Body, and an Editor can hide it without deleting any content.\n- [ ] Tests at the admin HTTP seam cover: Preview output matches the published-site output for the same Body (including sanitizing and an image with alt text); the hint appears in the Post editor, is not in the Body, and hiding it leaves the Body unchanged; and an Editor's Preview cannot be used to reach an Admin-only action.\n\n**Demo-ready and documented**\n\n- [ ] The demo seed rebuilds cleanly from `.env.example`: both roles, Published and Draft Posts and Pages, and one Deactivated account. It contains no real personal data and no claims about ASA beyond the brief.\n- [ ] A clean-clone smoke test runs the setup from `.env.example` plus the documented steps and reaches a working sign-in. No password, `.env` or database file is committed.\n- [ ] A release checklist covers `cms publish`, `cms deploy`, the relative-path check, adding approved image files, confirming Photo permission before a real photo is added, and the limit that an Editor cannot add an image file alone. It says that for the class demo the project author runs it, and does not claim ASA has an existing owner for this step or an approval process.\n- [ ] The README has Live URL, Run locally and Generative AI Use Statement sections, with the Backends used table.\n- [ ] Screenshots of the six admin screens (sign-in, dashboard, Content list, editor, users, and the permission-refusal page) at 1280 px and 390 px are saved in the screenshots folder.\n- [ ] The Stage 2 submission checker passes.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #5 (T04: blocking)\n- #7 (T06: blocking)\n- #8 (T07: blocking)\n\n\n## Follow-up from T01 (#2, commit 0cf7d23) — review before the demo release\n\n1. **Public fallback `CMS_SECRET_KEY`.** `app/settings.py` falls back to `\"dev-only-not-for-production\"` when the variable is unset, so session cookies would be signed with a key that is in the repo. Decide whether the app should refuse to start (or warn loudly) without a real key.\n2. **Well-known demo passwords in `.env.example`.** `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=change-me-admin` and `CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD=change-me-editor` pass the 8-character minimum, so `cms create-admin` and `scripts/seed_demo.py` will create accounts with those passwords if `.env` is copied unchanged. Consider rejecting the placeholder values, and make the release checklist say to change them.\n3. **Known limitation to review: replayed session cookies.** Sessions are stateless signed cookies (as the spec says). A copied cookie stays valid after sign-out until it expires (8 hours) or the account is Deactivated.
